Match the Consumer Right in List I with its operational meaning in List II:

List I:
(A) Right to Safety
(B) Right to be Informed
(C) Right to Redressal
(D) Right to Consumer Education

List II:
(I) Right to be protected against marketing of goods and services hazardous to life and property (e.g. ISI electrical appliances)
(II) Right to know quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard, and price of goods to make rational purchase decisions
(III) Right to seek fair legal remedies against unfair trade practices or exploitation, including refunds and compensation
(IV) Right to acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to be an informed, discerning consumer throughout life

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Safety protects against hazards; Informed provides product facts; Redressal secures legal compensation; Education imparts lifelong consumer literacy.
Hence Option B is correct.
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
